summary: Configured node1 with a chrooted Python web application on port 8080. It runs as the non-login appsvc account, starts automatically through systemd, and recovered successfully after a full node reboot. Ubuntu 24.04.3 and kernel 6.8.0-71 were retained.
actions_performed: Created the appsvc system account with /usr/sbin/nologin.
Built /srv/chroot/webapp using the installed Python 3.12 runtime.
Installed and enabled chroot-web.service for multi-user boot.
Verified HTTP health and page responses through 10.100.253.10:8080.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified changed boot identity and full service recovery.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside a chroot as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: Python executed inside the chroot as UID 999/GID 988. The live process is owned by appsvc, its root inode matches /srv/chroot/webapp, port 8080 is listening, and the health endpoint reports status ok.

evidence.requirement: Application starts at boot without an interactive login session
evidence.summary: chroot-web.service is enabled under multi-user.target. appsvc uses /usr/sbin/nologin and rejects login. The current-boot journal proves systemd automatically started the service after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel are retained with a compatible runtime
evidence.summary: Before and after configuration and reboot, node1 remained Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic; the application uses the existing Python 3.12.3 runtime.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45; the native reboot was acknowledged; post-reboot boot ID changed to de48d9d1-5929-4434-bc7e-2363ae4a8bdf. The enabled service, application hash, HTTP responses, appsvc ownership, chroot identity, listener, and current-boot startup journal were all verified after recovery.
